articles.title: Oklahoma Suffers Historic Upset Loss to East Texas A&M on 1st Day of CBB Season
articles.summary: Oklahoma basketball's season is off to a disastrous start.
articles.body:
Oklahoma basketball's season is off to a disastrous start.

The Sooners had what appeared to be an easy game against East Texas A&M in their season opener on Monday, but despite being 28.5-point favorites coming into the matchup, they dropped the game against the Lions.

It marked East Texas A&M's first-ever win against a power conference opponent and is the second-largest Division-I upset by spread in the last 30 years, according to ESPN.

East Texas A&M has never made the NCAA tournament and is coming off an 11-21 season, but the Lions perhaps could make history and make it to the Big Dance this year. A win over a Power 4 team will surely give them some momentum heading into the season.

Oklahoma, meanwhile, has some soul-searching to do after the historic loss.

The Sooners weren't favorites to compete for a title or win the SEC this year, but they were at least looking to get back into the NCAA tournament after missing last year.

Oklahoma will take on Mississippi Valley State on Friday, where it will look to avoid another historic upset.

articles.title: East Texas A&M stuns Oklahoma with historic road upset to open season, adding to Porter Moser's struggles in Norman
articles.summary: The Sooners were a 28.5-point favorite entering the night. Their loss is the second-largest upset in Division-I history in the past three decades.
articles.body:
It might be a long season for Porter Moser in Norman.

East Texas A&M stunned Oklahoma on Monday night to kick off the 2026-27 campaign. The Lions, who controlled most of the game, held on to grab a wild 68-64 upset win over the Sooners . It marked their first-ever win over a power conference program in history.

The Sooners closed as 28.5-point favorites, too. The upset, according to ESPN , is the second-largest in Division I in the past three decades. Eastern Illinois holds the record there after it beat Iowa as a 30.5-point underdog in 2022.

"The only thing I know what to do is apologize to the fan base, and to get better," Moser said, via The Oklahoman's Colton Sulley . "I apologize to every single person that came in. The things you do in a game like this in basketball that gets you beat, we did … Not good enough, and that's on me."

Oklahoma managed only 25 points in the first half, and hit just a single field goal in the final four minutes of the opening frame. The Lions, meanwhile, jumped up by 16 points after Mohamed Diakite and Alonzo Dodd drilled back-to-back 3-pointers out of the break.

Though the Sooners came back down the stretch, and Pop Isaacs cut it to a two-possession game with 25 seconds left after an and-one layup, that was as close as they got. Tyler Hendricks missed a 3-point look of his own that would have put them in the lead, and then Bo Aldrich sealed the win with a pair of free throws in the final seconds for the Lions.

Aldrich led the way with 22 points after he went 8-of-12 from the field. The Lions went 11-of-27 from the 3-point line, too, compared to the just 5-of-20 that Oklahoma did from distance. Isaacs led the Sooners with 15 points, and Derrion Reid added 14 points. They were the only two Oklahoma players to hit double figures.

The Lions are only in their sixth season of existence this fall. They've never had a winning record, and went just 13-20 in each of the past two seasons. They were selected to finish last in the Southland preseason poll, too.

Moser, on the other hand, might be in trouble in Norman. He is in his sixth season leading the Sooners this fall. While he has had some impressive moments in his career, including leading Loyola Chicago to the Final Four in 2018, he entered this season with just a 95-75 record at Oklahoma. They've never won an NCAA tournament game under his watch, have been to the tournament only once and have finished in the bottom of the SEC standings in their two seasons in that league.

Moser has just one year left on his contract with the Sooners after the 2026-27 season. Oklahoma has a new athletic director, Roger Denny, running the show now, too. If Moser can't turn things around quickly and lead the Sooners to the tournament after Monday's opening loss, it wouldn't be surprising to see Denny making a change this spring.

articles.title: Watch Draymond Green, Dillon Brooks Fight in Viral Video, Warriors Star Ejected vs. Suns
articles.summary: Draymond Green and Dillon Brooks have gotten into plenty of scuffles during their respective careers, and they went face-to-face during Monday's contest between the Golden State Warriors and Phoenix Suns.
articles.body:
Draymond Green and Dillon Brooks have gotten into plenty of scuffles during their respective careers, and they went face-to-face during Monday's contest between the Golden State Warriors and Phoenix Suns.

Green started the sequence that eventually led to his ejection by throwing Suns big man Khaman Maluach to the ground. Brooks took issue with it and approached Green, which caused the Warriors forward to grab his opponent's jersey near the throat:

The Michigan State product received two technical fouls and was ejected.

That it was Brooks and Green who got into it probably doesn't come as much of a surprise for NBA fans.

After all, Brooks led the league in technical fouls last season, while Green wasn't far behind in third. They both have reputations as players who never hesitate to trash talk and play with a physical approach on the defensive side, and that spilled over Monday.

"I don't like Draymond at all," Brooks said in a 2023 feature from ESPN's Tim Keown . Notably Keown added that Green "laughed and chose to pass on the opportunity to respond."

But he has since responded by calling Brooks an "idiot" and "sucker" in different instances .

They clearly still aren't fans of each other if Monday's fight was the latest indication, and it also wouldn't come as a surprise if Green has something to say about it on his next podcast.

And that will only set the stage for the next showdown when the Warriors face the Suns on Dec. 28.

articles.title: Warriors star Draymond Green ejected after throwing Khaman Maluach down, getting into scuffle with Dillon Brooks
articles.summary: Draymond Green was not happy after being knocked to the court on Monday night in San Francisco.
articles.body:
Draymond Green picked up his first ejection of the season on Monday night after he got into it with Dillon Brooks at the Chase Center.

The incident started after Green and Phoenix center Khaman Maluach got tangled up in the lane during the Warriors' 116-113 win over the Suns on Monday. That sparked the entire altercation in the third quarter. Maluach appeared to shake Green off and knock him to the ground early in the period, which left him wide open for a pass in the lane.

Green, clearly upset, jumped up immediately and grabbed Maluach as he was going up for the layup. Green kept going and threw Maluach down to the court.

Though things stopped for a moment after that, Brooks came running in to confront Green. The two got into it briefly under the basket before they were eventually separated.

Green was hit with two technical fouls and ejected, the first for throwing Maluach down and the second for his altercation with Brooks, who also received a technical foul for his role in the incident. It marked the first ejection of the season for Green, and the 23rd of his regular-season career.

Green finished the night with four points and four rebounds. The 36-year-old is in his 15th season in the league this fall.

Despite losing Green early, the Warriors surged back in the third quarter thanks to a 18-point period from Stephen Curry to get back into the contest. They then held on down the stretch to secure the three-point win.

Devin Booker led the Suns with 26 points in the loss, which dropped them to 1-4 on the year. Miles Bridges added 21 points, and Brooks finished with 18 points and eight rebounds.

Curry finished with 34 points, 7 assists and 6 rebounds for the Warriors. Brandin Podziemski added 20 points, and Charles Bassey finished with a career-high 19 points off the bench after he shot 7-of-10 from the field. The Warriors are now 5-3 this season.

While they ended up with the win, Green's latest ejection could cost him a suspension in the coming days.

articles.title: Spurs' five-game winning streak sets them apart from rest of NBA
articles.summary: The defending West champs now have six different winning streaks of five-plus games over the last two seasons, most of any NBA team.
articles.body:
The Spurs' 119-97 victory over Utah at the Frost Bank Center on Monday night hiked their winning streak to five games and gave them six different winning streaks of five-plus games over the last two seasons, most of any NBA team.

For the players who survived the back-to-back 22-win seasons in 2022-23 and 2023-24, it's quite an achievement.

"It's just a testament to pounding the rock," eighth-year forward Keldon Johnson said after finishing with 15 points and seven rebounds, both season highs for the reigning NBA Sixth Man of the Year.

"We continued to pound the rock (in those lean years). We continued to stay with it, and the tide turned. We just got to continue to build on those habits we have started. And every day keep coming in and putting our time in, putting that effort in, locking in and getting better each and every day."

Along those lines, Johnson believes the defending Western Conference champions have a long way to go until they hit their stride this season.

"Not comforting at all," Johnson said of the winning streak. "It's a long season, 82 games. We got to continue to get better. Do I feel as though we're playing to our standards? At times, yes. But do I feel like we could do better? Yes. I feel like we have a lot of room for improvement. I feel like we have not yet played our best brand of basketball and we just got to continue to stack days."

New York and Oklahoma City each have five different winning streaks of five-plus games over the last two seasons to rank second behind the Spurs, according to Elias Sports.

articles.title: ‘Least surprising ever’ – NBA fans sound off on Draymond Green vs. Dillon Brooks fight
articles.summary: Two of the NBA’s most volatile stars clashed during the Golden State Warriors’ clash against the Phoenix Suns, and fans online are far from surprised. Dillon...
articles.body:
Two of the NBA's most volatile stars clashed during the Golden State Warriors' clash against the Phoenix Suns, and fans online are far from surprised.

Dillon Brooks and Draymond Green are both known for their extremely heated temperaments which often result in volatile altercations on the court. With the Golden State Warriors taking on the Phoenix Suns on Monday night, an issue between the two was always a possibility.

Draymond Green was ejected from the Warriors' game against the Suns after a third-quarter issue between him and Brooks. In this scenario, the Golden State Warriors man was the aggressor, and naturally fans were quick to call him out online.

NBA fans blame Draymond Green for the fight between him and Dillon Brooks

The Golden State Warriors claimed the victory in the end, but they had to do it without their defensive anchor and offensive hub. Green was kicked out of the game for grabbing center Khaman Maluach in the air while making no play on the ball and then trying to choke Brooks when he showed up to confront him.

The referees gave Draymond two technicals and Brooks one for their exchange. The moment unsurprisingly went viral online.

"This is the least surprising thing ever, I should have bet my house on it," one fan claimed. "Dillon wasn't wrong, way to have your teammate back," a second fan said. "They need to get Draymond out of the league man, this dude is genuinely the worst," a third comment observed.

"What makes Draymond think he is so tough, like legit asking," a different reply read. "I can't believe I'm saying this but I am on Dillon Brooks' side here," a fifth fan said. "You can't convince me that Draymond Green does not need to get therapy mate," a sixth person wrote.

The Warriors managed to get the win even with the handicap but this is the latest in a line of extremely irresponsible behaviour from Green. It would not be surprising if his actions resulted in him being further disciplined by the NBA.

articles.title: Aday Mara, protagonista en la primera gran exhibición de Shai
articles.standfirst: El pívot español firma un 10+9 en la victoria de los Thunder en Cleveland
articles.summary: El pívot español firma un 10+9 en la victoria de los Thunder en Cleveland
articles.body: Los Thunder van a tener que tomar serias medidas de dosificación con su gran estrella y el jugador que les va a sostener toda la temporada. Shai Gilgeous-Alexander acabó completamente agotado en su primera gran exhibición del año que permitió a su equipo ganar en Cleveland, 112-117, en una exigente visita ya que fue la primera derrota de los Cavs en casa en cuatro partidos. Shai tuvo que exprimirse a fondo: 43 puntos, su tope de la temporada, en 39 minutos con la friolera de 35 lanzamientos a canasta, casi a uno por minuto. Nadie, en dos semanas de competición, había tirado tanto. Es un récord producto de las ausencias en los Thunder y una muestra de lo que les espera en la temporada. Está claro que para ganar, Shai necesita ayuda en su equipo y esta le llegó desde el banquillo. Aday Mara jugando 20 minutos, cuarto partido seguido que está en pista al menos 20 minutos, aportó 10 puntos y nueve rebotes con un 5/7 en tiros de campo. Fue el segundo jugador de la segunda unidad que más estuvo en pista por detrás de Jared McCain (27 minutos, para siete puntos y nueve rebotes). En realidad Mara fue el cuarto mejor anotar de su equipo. Shai, claro, puso el listón con esos 43 puntos, seguidos de los 20 de Ajay Mitchell y los 12 de Kenrich Williams. Gilgeous-Alexander firmó un triple milagroso a 32 segundos para el final para sellar el triunfo de su equipo en Cleveland. Los Cavs aguantaron vivos casi hasta ese triple de Shai. Lo tuvieron cerca y vendieron cara su primera derrota en casa. Donovan Mitchell y el rookie Maleek Thomas, en su primera titularidad, lideraron la ofensiva de los locales con 17 puntos. Mario Hezonja, 27 minutos desde el banquillo, acabó con 12 puntos, ocho rebotes y tres asistencias con 4/9 en tiros de campo y 3/7 en triples. Los Thunder recuperaron la senda de la victoria tras dos derrotas (Dallas y Houston), pero tuvieron que exprimir a su gran líder para llevarse el partido. Será una tónica toda la temporada ante las muchas ausencias que tendrán.

articles.title: Young state star impresses in his UWM debut as the Panthers fall to USC
articles.summary: The Panthers opened against a ranked opponent with 7-footers, but found bright spots in the play of a freshman and their resilience.
articles.body:
For a mid-major team looking to bounce back from a miserable 2025-26 season, starting on the road against a ranked opponent with 7-footers in the middle was a tough ask.

That's what the Milwaukee Panthers did, though, on opening night of college basketball season Nov. 2 and they suffered the sort of fate one might expect, a 95-63 loss to Southern California at the Galen Center in Los Angeles in the teams' first meeting.

The Trojans, ranked 22 nd in USA Today coaches poll, used a size advantage that included 7-foot freshmen Adonis and Darius Ratliff, sons of former NBA player Theo Ratliff, and pulled away with a 19-2 run in the first half.

"Anybody that wasn't here live, you don't understand is how much length and positional size they have," UWM coach Bart Lundy said in his postgame radio interview. "It's basically an NBA team. There's gonna be five guys on that team that are gonna play in the NBA, and a couple might be really good NBA players.

Our favorite photos from UWM men's basketball in 2025-26

"The combination of athleticism, size, and skill is pretty amazing. … That's an unusual team. They're better than 21st in the country."

Adonis Ratliff led the Trojans with 25 points as well as six rebounds and went 5 of 7 from 3-point range. Sophomore guard Alijah Arenas, son of Gilbert Arenas, had 21 points and a team-high eight rebounds.

Freshman guard Amare Hereford was a bright spot for Milwaukee, which is looking to bounce back from an injury-plagued 12-20 season. The top scorer in Wisconsin high school basketball last season and Beloit Memorial's all-time leader led the Panthers with 14 points in 26 minutes.

Marquette transfer guard Tre Norman added all 13 of his points in the second half for the Panthers and Isiah Dorceus, one of five returning Panthers, scored 10 in 15 points.

"Those three figured out they could get downhill and make plays for themselves and for others," said Lundy, who began his fifth season at UWM. "And that's what we've seen in practice.

"It's just … we were in a huge deficit, and then the 3s. ... I really thought for a little bit that we were going to make a comeback run."

Jake Hansen, a Wauwatosa West graduate who played three games at Oklahoma last season, hit a pair of 3-pointers in the first half and scored eight points but was limited by foul trouble.

For UWM, USC marked the first of five nonconference opponents who are ranked or received votes in preseason polls. The Panthers stay in California for a Nov. 4 matchup at Santa Clara.

articles.title: Young state star impresses in his UWM debut as the Panthers fall to USC
articles.summary: The Panthers opened against a ranked opponent with 7-footers, but found bright spots in the play of a freshman and their resilience.
articles.body:
For a mid-major team looking to bounce back from a miserable 2025-26 season, starting on the road against a ranked opponent with 7-footers in the middle was a tough ask.

That's what the Milwaukee Panthers did, though, on opening night of college basketball season Nov. 2 and they suffered the sort of fate one might expect, a 95-63 loss to Southern California at the Galen Center in Los Angeles in the teams' first meeting.

The Trojans, ranked 22 nd in USA Today coaches poll, used a size advantage that included 7-foot freshmen Adonis and Darius Ratliff, sons of former NBA player Theo Ratliff, and pulled away with a 19-2 run in the first half.

"Anybody that wasn't here live, you don't understand is how much length and positional size they have," UWM coach Bart Lundy said in his postgame radio interview. "It's basically an NBA team. There's gonna be five guys on that team that are gonna play in the NBA, and a couple might be really good NBA players.

Our favorite photos from UWM men's basketball in 2025-26

"The combination of athleticism, size, and skill is pretty amazing. … That's an unusual team. They're better than 21st in the country."

Adonis Ratliff led the Trojans with 25 points as well as six rebounds and went 5 of 7 from 3-point range. Sophomore guard Alijah Arenas, son of Gilbert Arenas, had 21 points and a team-high eight rebounds.

Freshman guard Amare Hereford was a bright spot for Milwaukee, which is looking to bounce back from an injury-plagued 12-20 season. The top scorer in Wisconsin high school basketball last season and Beloit Memorial's all-time leader led the Panthers with 14 points in 26 minutes.

Marquette transfer guard Tre Norman added all 13 of his points in the second half for the Panthers and Isiah Dorceus, one of five returning Panthers, scored 10 in 15 points.

"Those three figured out they could get downhill and make plays for themselves and for others," said Lundy, who began his fifth season at UWM. "And that's what we've seen in practice.

"It's just … we were in a huge deficit, and then the 3s. ... I really thought for a little bit that we were going to make a comeback run."

Jake Hansen, a Wauwatosa West graduate who played three games at Oklahoma last season, hit a pair of 3-pointers in the first half and scored eight points but was limited by foul trouble.

For UWM, USC marked the first of five nonconference opponents who are ranked or received votes in preseason polls. The Panthers stay in California for a Nov. 4 matchup at Santa Clara.

articles.title: Dave Portnoy accuses 76ers’ LeBron James of setting a poor example with mid-game wine sip
articles.summary: LeBron James is approaching the age of 42 and is enjoying every single second he has left on an NBA court. On Monday night, in the third quarter of the Phila...
articles.body:
LeBron James is approaching the age of 42 and is enjoying every single second he has left on an NBA court. On Monday night, in the third quarter of the Philadelphia 76ers ' 126-107 victory over the Chicago Bulls, he continued his quirky era by taking a sip of wine from a fan's cup in the middle of the game after he ran all the way to the baseline on a botched possession.

This was a lighthearted moment that drew some laughter at Xfinity Mobile Arena, as it is becoming very evident that James is playing loose and carefree and does not care that much at all anymore about what other people think. However, this wine-sipping "incident", so to speak, has become a reason for some, including Barstool Sports owner Dave Portnoy, to dish out some criticism the 76ers star's way.

Portnoy, in a rant on his X account, accused James of setting a poor example for children after he consumed alcohol in the middle of an NBA game.

"If anybody else did this they'd be checked into AA but because it's Bron Bron Sportcenter will do an hour special on it. Who cares the example it sets for kids that you need to be drunk to play sports?" Portnoy wrote.

Drinking while on the job is a frowned-upon practice in workplaces, so it's a bit understandable as to where Portnoy is coming from. If a regular employee drank while on the job in a corporate setting, he might have been on the unemployment line the next morning.

However, the NBA isn't exactly a regular job, and no one could get drunk from a single sip of an alcoholic beverage. Portnoy is being a bit overdramatic by insinuating that the 76ers star could get anywhere close to being inebriated after taking that little amount of wine.

This just proves that James, no matter what he does, is always going to be one of, if not outright the most divisive superstar of his generation .
